notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/08/2025
Patient: Candelaria Greenholt, 69-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 04/08/2025. The study assessed the patient's sleep patterns and breathing abnormalities during sleep. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 40.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 7% of all events. The majority of respiratory events were obstructive in nature. Oxygen saturation showed intermittent drops corresponding to apnea and hypopnea episodes. Sleep architecture revealed normal distribution of sleep stages with frequent arousals related to respiratory disturbances. These findings are consistent with severe sleep apnea. Recommendations include evaluation for positive airway pressure therapy and follow-up with a sleep specialist.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 08/25/2026
Patient: Candelaria Greenholt, 70-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Ms. Greenholt is a 70-year-old female with a history of obstructive sleep apnea currently on CPAP therapy. She reports ongoing symptoms despite treatment.

Physical Examination:
BMI 31.5 kg/m2.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP failure: residual AHI 23.3 events/hour on CPAP at 10 cmH2O despite consistent nightly use.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates persistent moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea despite adherence to CPAP therapy at prescribed pressure settings.

Plan:
1. Consider reassessment of CPAP settings and possible titration.
2. Evaluate for alternative therapies including oral appliance or advanced PAP modalities.
3. Reinforce adherence and proper mask fit.
4. Schedule follow-up sleep study to assess treatment efficacy.
5. Continue monitoring comorbid conditions and overall sleep quality.

Summary:
Ms. Greenholt's obstructive sleep apnea remains inadequately controlled on current CPAP therapy. Further evaluation and treatment adjustments are warranted to optimize outcomes.
